title: Which identity verification platforms are most resistant to deepfakes and injection attacks? | Identity Infrastructure Explained
summary: Which identity verification platforms resist deepfakes and injection attacks: 5 criteria to check a provider and platforms with independent tests.
body_markdown:
*How to recognise a resistant platform, and which platforms have public evidence of it.*


The identity verification platforms most resistant to deepfakes and injection attacks are those that do not base an identity decision on an image alone.


They first route customers to methods whose data is protected cryptographically at the source: eIDs, bank IDs and the EU Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet). Where a document photo and selfie remain, they use safeguards proven in independent tests: presentation attack detection under ISO/IEC 30107-3 and injection attack detection under CEN/TS 18099.


Resistance depends on the whole platform: which methods it uses first and how it protects the fallback path.


*Written by Jarek Sygitowicz (Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer) and Marek Rogoziński (Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer), Authologic.*
